sections.title: The Burning Bush
observations: In this pivotal moment, Moses encounters God in the form of a burning bush that is not consumed by the fire. This miraculous sight captures Moses' attention and signifies God's presence. It is a profound reminder that God is holy and must be approached with reverence.
God's call to Moses marks the beginning of a significant mission. The burning bush symbolizes God's desire to reveal Himself and His plans to His people.

sections.title: God's Commission to Moses
observations: God reveals His plan to deliver the Israelites from slavery in Egypt. He chooses Moses as the instrument for this deliverance, highlighting God's sovereignty in choosing unlikely leaders for His purposes.
Moses' initial reluctance and questions reflect a common human response to God's calling. This section emphasizes the importance of faith and obedience in responding to God's call.

sections.title: God's Name Revealed
observations: God reveals His name to Moses as 'I AM WHO I AM,' indicating His eternal, self-sufficient nature. This revelation is foundational for understanding God's character and His relationship with His people.
The name signifies God's unchanging presence and His commitment to fulfill His promises, providing assurance to Moses and the Israelites.

sections.title: Moses' Objections and God's Assurance
observations: Moses raises several objections regarding his ability to lead the Israelites. God's responses demonstrate His patience and the provision of signs to validate Moses' mission.
This dialogue illustrates the tension between human inadequacy and divine empowerment, emphasizing that God equips those He calls.

importantVerses.commentary: God's declaration of His name, 'I AM WHO I AM,' is crucial for understanding His nature and the assurance it provides to His people.
God's promise to be with Moses underscores the theme of divine presence throughout the narrative of Exodus.

questions: What does the burning bush symbolize in the context of God's revelation to Moses?
How does God's self-identification as 'I AM' shape our understanding of His nature?
What can we learn from Moses' objections about our own responses to God's calling?
In what ways does this chapter prepare us for the themes of deliverance and covenant in the rest of Exodus?
